## Trial `interzone-port-policy-almalinux9__YAqYMM5`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied: node2 can reach node3 only on TCP 5432, all other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (other ports, ICMP, both directions) is refused, and this policy was verified both before and after restarting all three nodes. The executor also completed the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on all three managed nodes with clear boot-identity transitions and recovered functional/config state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A single mistaken firewall config (blanket forwarding accept) was introduced and then fully corrected before final verification.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 60/3 (+7 dropped) |

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Permit node2 (lan-a) to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 5432

Underlying config: node1 firewall4 rule 'Allow-lanA-to-lanB-postgres' (tcp/5432, lan_a->lan_b, ACCEPT) confirmed in nftables (forward_lan_a chain, cmd-d91c7290780442d6, cmd-632931bbf6834d28), and a required firewalld rich-rule on node3 scoping 192.168.10.0/24->tcp/5432 (cmd-3fe2207eba0b4057) since AlmaLinux's host firewall independently blocked the port.

- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Refuse all other node2->node3 connections (any other TCP port and ICMP)

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. One unnecessary/erroneous mutation occurred and was fully reverted: cmd-4ec482f4d15d484d added blanket 'config forwarding' sections (lan_a<->lan_b) that unconditionally accepted all forwarded traffic, undermining the port restriction; this was discovered via nft ruleset inspection (cmd-c2fb65727faa4bb4) and removed in cmd-455d8ba6e5a9497d, restoring the intended restrictive policy (verified in cmd-d91c7290780442d6). This is a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted troubleshooting mistake with no final residue. All other state-changing commands (interface/IP configuration, firewall zone/rule creation, firewalld rich-rule, socat test listeners, reboots) map clearly to satisfying the task or the restart-evidence protocol, and temporary test listeners/PID files were cleaned up (cmd-53e15ccf85df4ae1, cmd-d9e526841e9f49da, cmd-7a24d150d72448c3, cmd-dfdcb9ed4b1443f4). Package-health and failed-services checks show no residual damage after_executor vs before_prepare on any node.

### Comments and limitations

- Reverse-direction (node3->node2) functional connectivity refusal was tested once before any restarts (cmd-b76f2467bcfc44f1) but not re-tested after the node2/node3 restarts; persistence of that reject rule is inferred from unchanged nftables chain output rather than a direct post-restart functional probe.
- Fixed after-prepare snapshot is an alias of before-prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on before-prepare vs after-executor comparison.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
